Avoid Dehydration Drinking: Avoid dehydration by drinking plenty of fluids andeating enough throughout the day to keep your body well-balanced.
Youbecome Weary Develop: If youbecome weary or develop a headache or body aches, or if you becomeconfused, rest in the shade and sip water until the symptoms subside.
Freezing Continues Area: If the freezing continues, the area will stiffen andbecome grayish-white in color.
step_by_step_procedure: Thaw Theaffected Area: To treat the victim, thaw theaffected area only if there is no risk of refreezing.
Cold Fingers Armpit: Put cold fingers under the armpit and the warm palm of your hand on frostbitten nose, ears, or cheeks.
Shelter Possible Cold: In a shelter, if possible, put cold feet on a companion’s barebelly, or immerse the affected area in lukewarm water, nowarmer than 108 degrees.
Blisters Develop Apply: If blisters develop, apply a large steriledressing.

step_by_step_procedure: Loosely Loop Rope: Loosely loop one rope end twice aroundthe other, then thread the end of that rope through the loops.
Carefully Tightenthe Parts: Carefully tightenthe two parts of the knot, then slide them against each other.
They Don Fit: If they don’t fit together neatly, the knot is incorrectly tied.
Knot Commonlytied Accessory: The knot is commonlytied with accessory cord by a climber to ascend a rope or to secure abelay system in order to release the belayer.

There-fore Learnhow Tie: There-fore, you must learnhow to tie a seat harness from a qualified instructor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Verbal Signals Climbers: Verbal Signals for Climbers and Belayers Verbal signals allow a climber and a belayer to communicate and worktogether as a team even if they cannot.
Habit Ofusing Verbal: Get in the habit ofusing verbal signals every time you are climbing or belaying.
Arrange Rope Stronger: Arrange the rope so that your stronger hand (usually your right hand if you are right-handed) will be the brake hand, thehand closest to the free end.
Exchange Verbalsignals Boxed: Exchange verbalsignals (see the boxed text later in this chapter) with a climber.
step_by_step_procedure: Climber Ascends Pull: As the climber ascends, pull through the belay device any slackthat forms in the rope, and let the loose rope pile up next to your feet.
Holding Rope Firmly: While holding the rope firmly with your brake hand, slideyour guide hand out along the rope.
Slack Rope Minimum: Keeping slack in the rope to a minimum will limit thelength of a fall if the climber slips.
Running Rope Belay: Running the rope through a belay deviceallows a belayer to stop a fall easily, justby moving the belay rope to one side.
